title: The Relationship Between Macbeth and Lady Macbeth
author: Dominic Salles
summary: Dominic Salles presents a model grade 8 GCSE essay on the relationship between Macbeth and Lady Macbeth and annotates it to show what examiners reward. The essay argues that Shakespeare portrays a controlling marriage in which both spouses manipulate each other, using imperative verbs, Lady Macbeth's questioning, the letter written in prose rather than iambic pentameter, and Macbeth's cold reaction to her death. Salles then compares the counts that separate a grade 5 essay from a grade 8, such as quotes, named methods, references to society and patriarchy, and mentions of Shakespeare's purpose. He argues that students can move up quickly by learning Shakespeare's ideas and by working through the extract chronologically so the letter is not missed. He also shares examiner comments and AI marking feedback, and the post includes promotional codes for the Tilf marking tool.
points: Salles counts features of essays at each grade, showing that a grade 5 response needs a thesis and conclusion but little exploratory language or discussion of the author's ideas.
Referring to Shakespeare's purpose and to society and patriarchy is presented as the cheapest way to climb a grade, requiring perhaps ten minutes of learning.
The model essay earns credit by analysing the letter in prose versus iambic pentameter, a point many students miss because they start with the extract rather than working chronologically.
Students are advised to harvest impressive vocabulary from model answers and practise writing their own sentences with it to explain quotations.
AI marking feedback is framed as most useful for how-to-improve advice rather than for the exact mark, since examiners themselves only give the right grade about half the time.
quotes: An argument needs lots of evidence, and that means lots of quotes. So, even at grade 5, students average 10 quotes per essay.

You do not need to write about the author’s ideas - this is why the essay only mentions Shakespeare once. This is the easiest way to move up the grades - learning what Shakespeare’s ideas are in the play is 10 minutes work, maximum.
Notice how writing about the letter, and the language of power, has really impressed the examiner.
So a good way to revise is to write down the words which impress you. Put the essay aside, and try to write your own sentences using those words to explain any quotation.
However, he writes to her in PROSE rather than in IAMBIC PENTAMETER. This challenges our perceptions that the relationship is between equals.
If you work through the question chronologically, the letter will be relevant to 100% of essays about Lady Macbeth, or the marriage, and probably about 70% of the questions on Macbeth himself.

In conclusion, Shakespeare portrays the relationship as controlling. He uses language and structure to show both spouses manipulate each other and seek to dominate, which leads to their loveless marriage and finally to their deaths.
